(1) complex function words are often considered as pre-tokenized units in parsing, but they can be ambiguous; (2) we propose a model for parsing and identification of such complex function words; and (3) we train the model on a modified version (including morphological dependency information) of the French TreeBank, and evaluate it on two tasks: (a) recognition of ADV+que and (b) de+DET.

we have developed a new model for joint parsing and multiword expression tokenization, that it outperforms a standard parser on a modified French Treebank with morphological dependencies, and that it is able to recognize a significant number of complex function words.

1) the joint dependency parsing and MWE tokenization model is a good approach for MWE identification, 2) it is better than the traditional approach, and 3) the MWE tokenization is a good preprocessing step for the joint parsing model.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problems: (i) the identification of complex function words, (ii) the integration of this identification into a parsing model, and (iii) the evaluation of the resulting joint parsing and tokenization.

the following questions: How can we improve the performance of dependency parsing by taking into account morphological dependencies? How can we improve morphological parsing by taking into consideration syntactic information?

the model we propose is able to jointly identify multiword expressions and to perform a syntactic analysis of a sentence, with an acceptable performance.
the results are promising, and the model is a viable alternative to pretokenization.

the model is able to recognize a high percentage of multiword expressions with high precision, and that the parser is able to learn the correct syntactic dependencies between the individual tokens of these multiword expressions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that a joint model of MWE identification and dependency parsing is feasible, and it is a step forward in the right direction.
the proposed model is able to identify complex function words and their dependencies with a high degree of accuracy.
the joint model performs better than the single models, and the joint parser is better than the single parsers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the joint model outperforms the standard model in which complex function tokens are pretokenized.
complex function words can be identified and parsed with high precision, even in a fully unsupervised way.
